newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon cement maker readies $50 mln bond.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon cement maker readies $50 mln bond.

text.p: Shareholders of Societe des Ciments Libanais approved on Thursday a resolution authorising a bond issue of up to $50 million.
The issue, with a term of up to 10 years, will carry interest at 3.875 percent over six-months LIBOR, the resolution said.

Shareholders approved the resolution at their annual meeting at the company's headquarters at Chekka north of Beirut. It said the bonds could be issued either on the Lebanese market or the Euro-market.
If issued on the Euro-market it will be the second $50 million Eurobond issued by SCL, Lebanon's biggest cement producer.
SCL issued a $50 million Eurobond in January 1996 to help finance its modernisation programme, including construction of a new kiln due to start production in July or August.
Shareholders granted the board the option to make the issue in one or several tranches.
According to the company's annual report, the issue will be used to repay a $35 million bridging loan taken out last December with a syndicate headed by Banque Libano-Francaise.
SCL undertook to issue the bond by July 1, the report said.
